title: Palo Alto NGFW or Forcepoint NGFW: Application Control vs Built-In Data Protection
excerpt: Both are enterprise next-generation firewalls, but they start from different places. Palo Alto is built around identifying applications and users for fine-grained policy; Forcepoint has long treated data loss prevention as part of the firewall rather than an add-on.
verdict: Pick Palo Alto if you want the larger user community, broad integration with other security tools and very granular application-level policy. Pick Forcepoint if data loss prevention is a core requirement, as it often is in government and finance, or if you prefer its management model. Review sites show Palo Alto with a much larger base of user reviews and a slightly higher average rating, but that reflects market reach more than quality; both are established enterprise products. Neither vendor publishes list prices, so get quotes for your real throughput and subscription bundle before comparing cost.
